title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page belongs to 'Variations sur l'équation des lacets', the sequel to La Longue Marche. There Grothendieck studies automorphisms of the profinite completions of π_{0,3} and SL(2,Z) (a free product with amalgamation Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6). He restricts to automorphisms that respect the inertia/parabolic subgroups and the torsion elements ρ (order 3 or 6) and σ (order 2 or 4). Such automorphisms are encoded by 'invariants' α, β, γ, ζ, η, μ, ε, ε'. These invariants are packaged as points of a group scheme M_{ρ,σ}. On the preceding page this group is described as a subgroup of T_0 × T_ρ × N'_σ, namely triples (u, a, b) with det u = det b = ε' det a. Here T_0 is the torus or Borel attached to the cusp 0, T_ρ the torus attached to ρ, and N'_σ the normaliser of the torus attached to σ. On p. 403, formula (35), he introduced three 'anti-involutions' of GL(2,Z) of determinant −1, playing the role of complex conjugations: Γ_0 = τ'_∞ = [[0,1],[1,0]], Γ_1 = −τ'_0 = [[−1,1],[0,1]], Γ_∞ = τ_∞ = diag(−1,1). On this page he begins computing the invariants and the triple (u, a, b) for each of them.

Case Γ_∞ = τ_∞ = diag(−1,1) ∈ GL(2,Z) ⊂ GL(2,Ẑ)^{±1}:
- τ_∞ is the unique non-trivial element of T'_0(Z) ≅ G_m(Z) = {±1}.
- Conjugation by τ_∞ sends [[a,b],[c,d]] to [[a,−b],[−c,d]]. It therefore normalises the cusp subgroup L̃_0 generated by ε_0 = [[1,1],[0,1]], and its index-2 subgroup generated by l_0 = ε_0^2. It inverts both: τ_∞(ε_0) = ε_0^{-1} and τ_∞(l_0) = l_0^{-1}.
- Hence τ_∞ lies in M_{0,3}^{!~}[0], the automorphisms 'of type 0', i.e. adapted to the cusp 0.
- Writing τ_∞ = u_{α,β}, earlier computations give α = τ_∞ and ζ = g = αρ(α)^{-1} = −l_1^{-1} = −[[1,0],[−2,1]]. He warns about the sign: the computation must be done in SL(2,Z), not in the commutator subgroup SL(2,Z)'.
- Further, β = 1, η = h = 1, μ = −1, ε = ε_2(μ) = −1 and ε' = ε_3(μ) = −1.
- With B = 0 and D = −1, the Borel element is u = [[1/D, B/D],[0,1]] = diag(−1,1) = τ_∞.
- Then a = α^{-1}u = 1 and b = β^{-1}u = τ_∞, the non-trivial 2-torsion element.
- Result (36): Γ_∞ ↦ (u_∞ = τ_∞, a_∞ = 1, b_∞ = τ_∞) ∈ T_0 × T_ρ × N'_σ.

The NB generalises to any upper-triangular u = [[μ,λ],[0,1]] in the Borel B'_0(Ẑ). It asks for the invariants of the automorphism that u induces on the completed SL(2,Z)^{!~} and on B̂^+_{0,3}. The next page answers: (u, 1, τ_∞^k) with μ = (−1)^k. This gives Γ_1 at once, and Γ_0 = τ_∞σ_∞ is then obtained as a product.

Purpose: to locate the 'real structures' (complex-conjugation-like elements) inside his group M_{ρ,σ}, so as to extend the GT-type theory of the profinite modular group to GL(2) with orientation-reversing elements. This is the analogue of adjoining complex conjugation to the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group.
errors: In the formula u = (1/D = μ, B/D = μD) the entry B/D should be μB, since μ = 1/D. This is harmless here because B = 0.
The NB writes B'_0(Ẑ) ⊂ Gl(2,Z); it should be Gl(2,Ẑ), or the Z-points.
Minor: the sign subtlety ζ = −l_1^{-1} is flagged by Grothendieck himself (SL(2,Z) versus SL(2,Z)'). The computation itself checks out: conjugation by diag(−1,1) does invert ε_0 = [[1,1],[0,1]].

ideas.what: Orientation-reversing involutions Γ_0, Γ_1, Γ_∞ of determinant −1 in GL(2,Z), each fixing a cusp. They generate GL(2,Z) (or its commutator-related subgroup), act by outer automorphisms on the profinite modular group and π_{0,3}, and behave like complex conjugations.
ideas.modern_name: Real structures / complex conjugation acting on the profinite modular group; GL(2,Z) as the extended modular group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical for GL(2,Z) (extended modular group). The profinite and GT setting with complex conjugation appears in Drinfeld (1990), Ihara, and Lochak–Schneps.
ideas.where_published: Possibly alluded to in La Longue Marche; not in Esquisse in this form

ideas.what: Parametrisation of cusp-adapted automorphisms of the profinite SL(2,Z) by triples (u, a, b) in T_0 × T_ρ × N'_σ, with a determinant condition coupling them. The elliptic points ρ and σ and the cusp each carry a torus or normaliser.
ideas.modern_name: Description of a GT-like group of automorphisms of profinite SL(2,Z) via local data at elliptic points and cusps (inertia-preserving automorphisms)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Related work: Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps, Nakamura on GT acting on profinite modular groups (1990s–2000s)

ideas.what: Explicit computation that diag(−1,1) gives the triple (τ_∞, 1, τ_∞). The general Borel element [[μ,λ],[0,1]] gives (u, 1, τ_∞^k) with μ = (−1)^k.

missed.claim: Grothendieck's group M_{ρ,σ} ⊂ T_0 × T_ρ × N'_σ is a 'torus-type' model of cusp- and elliptic-point-adapted automorphisms of profinite SL(2,Z). He also embeds the anti-holomorphic involutions into it. This framework for a GL(2)/real-structure extension of GT acting on the profinite modular group does not appear, in this form, in the published GT literature.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could give a concrete local-data parametrisation of an extended GT^± acting on the profinite completion of GL(2,Z). Its usefulness depends on whether the full construction on surrounding pages is coherent; this page alone is a routine computation within it.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful but routine verification within Grothendieck's private framework (the group M_{ρ,σ}). The underlying theme, complex conjugation and GL(2,Z) acting on the profinite modular group alongside GT, is broadly known. The specific torus-triple formalism is unpublished, but this page adds only bookkeeping.
transcription_corrections: 'r_0, r_1, r_∞' is most likely Γ_0, Γ_1, Γ_∞, the anti-involutions named in (35) on the previous page.
In the formula for u, the entry is written 'B/D = μD' (with a correction); mathematically it should read μB.
'B'_0(Ẑ) ⊂ Gl(2,Z)': the hat is visible over Z on the left only; the inclusion should be into Gl(2,Ẑ).
The inserted phrase reads 'l'élément non trivial de ₂T_0(Z) ≃ ₂T_0(Z)'; the second factor may be ₂T_σ or ₂N'_σ (uncertain).
Archive page number 404, written at the bottom left; Grothendieck's own numbering is around 503/503'.
